_comment: Support knowledge, not code. Derived from the structure of a real public corpus, with fictional product names. Tell Claude what to change in plain words.
_derivation: Problem types come from the real troubleshooting article inventory. Required facts come from the branch points inside those articles and from documented OS and licence prerequisites.

problem_types.label: Login screen does not appear

facts.product: Each product serves its interface differently.
facts.os: The service check differs: a Windows service versus a Linux process.
facts.ssl_enabled: With SSL on, the address is https on a different port; with it off, plain http. Giving the wrong one looks like an outage.
facts.port_changed: A changed web port must be appended to the address, or the page never loads.

problem_types.derived_from: ref-190906_02, whose own steps branch on exactly these two settings

problem_types.label: Service will not start

facts.version: The Java requirement changed between versions, and a mismatched JDK stops startup.
facts.os: Windows runs it as a service; Linux as a process from a shell script.
facts.recent_change: A failure after an upgrade points at the upgrade; one on a new install points at setup.

problem_types.derived_from: ref-190906_01 (Windows), the JDK change in v1.8.0, and the verified-JDK article

problem_types.label: Service will not stop, or a process remains

facts.os: The stop path is a script on Linux and a service on Windows.
facts.recent_change: A firewall rule added for an unrelated fix is a known cause of this.

problem_types.derived_from: lsc_systemstopped (firewalld direct rule) and snp-190206_01 (stop/start sequencing)

problem_types.label: Logs are not arriving

facts.product: Log collection is not in every product or tier.
facts.licence_tier: Syslog and WMI collection are absent from some paid tiers. Check the licence before troubleshooting.
facts.collection_method: Syslog, WMI, FTP, SCP and REST API each have their own article and their own failure modes.
facts.os: Linux syslog collection needs root; Linux WMI collection needs the wmi package.

device_vendor.why: Some devices have their own article for why their logs do not arrive.

depends_on.prefix: If the logs come by syslog or SNMP from a network device:
depends_on.only_when: the logs come by syslog or SNMP from a network device

facts.recent_change: Collection that stopped after an upgrade is a different investigation from one that never started.

problem_types.derived_from: ref-230608_01, ref-191031_02, the nine per-method collection articles, and the OS prerequisites on the spec page

problem_types.label: Monitoring returns no data

facts.product: Monitoring is not in every product or tier.
facts.licence_tier: Port monitoring is paid-only; some monitoring is absent from log-only tiers.
facts.version: The 'acquisition failed' status was replaced by caution and warning in v2.4.4, so older guidance describes a status that no longer exists.
facts.device_vendor: Vendor-specific articles exist for the common firewalls.

snmp_version.why: SNMP v1 is not enough for the item scan; v2 or above is required.

problem_types.derived_from: ref-191031_01, snp-191119_01, ref-200825_01 (paid only), and the v2.4.4 status change

problem_types.label: Monitoring item scan finds nothing

facts.snmp_version: The scan needs SNMP v2 or above on the target.
facts.device_vendor: Community string and MIB support vary by device.

problem_types.derived_from: snp-191119_01, whose checklist is exactly these

problem_types.label: Disk space exhausted on the collector host

facts.os: The cleanup procedure has separate Windows and Linux articles.
facts.version: Moving the log directory was impossible before v2.0.0, so the answer depends on the version.
facts.licence_tier: Free-tier retention is fixed at 10 days, which changes what can be freed.

problem_types.derived_from: ref-190725_01 and _02 (the OS pair), snp-191031_03 (the v2.0.0 boundary)

facts.product: The licence model differs per product: per server, per device, or per user.
facts.licence_tier: What is restricted depends on the tier.

problem_types.label: Is this feature available to me?

facts.licence_tier: Availability is per licence tier. Most of these are answerable from the capability table with no search at all.

problem_types.derived_from: the feature matrices on the spec page and in the brochures

problem_types.label: How to upgrade, and what it depends on

facts.product: Each product has its own upgrade path and its own release notes.
facts.version: The version they are on now decides which upgrade steps apply and which release notes to read.
facts.os: The upgrade procedure differs between Windows and Linux.

problem_types.derived_from: real inquiry, 17 November 2026: how do I upgrade from 2.4.0 to 2.9.1, does it have dependencies

problem_types.label: A licence or capacity limit has been reached

facts.licence_tier: The limit IS the licence: the free tier allows 10 devices, the paid tiers allow more. This is the answer, not a step towards it.
facts.device_count: The current count against the limit says whether this needs a licence change or a configuration fix.

problem_types.derived_from: real inquiry, 17 November 2026: 1000 devices registered, how do I increase it to 1001

problem_types.label: How something works, or what a format is

facts.product: The answer comes from that product's own specification page.

problem_types.derived_from: real inquiry, 17 November 2026: how does syslog work and what is the log format

unknown_fallback.product: Needed for any problem, whatever it turns out to be.
unknown_fallback.version: Needed for any problem, whatever it turns out to be.

evidence_rules.what: A document whose body is only a pointer to another article carries no evidence. Follow the pointer or discard it.
evidence_rules.why: 12 of 18 specification articles in the real corpus are stubs of exactly this kind, and they remain indexed.

evidence_rules.what: A document stating only a lower bound ('from v1.7.0') is not evidence that it still applies to the current version. Treat its applicability as open, not as current.
evidence_rules.why: No article in the real corpus states an upper bound, so 'it does not say it stopped applying' carries no information.

evidence_rules.what: Where a newer document or release note contradicts an older claim, the claim is superseded even when the older document is still published.
evidence_rules.why: Two specification articles are actively false for current versions and say so only in an appended note.

evidence_rules.what: A document with no OS label does not apply to both. Its applicability is unknown and must be established another way.
evidence_rules.why: 46 of 105 reference articles state neither a version nor an OS.

evidence_rules.what: Do not use the published age banner as a staleness signal. Use the release history instead: a document is suspect when a release after its last update changed what it describes.
evidence_rules.why: The banner says it counts from the posting date but is computed from the last update, and understates age by years.

evidence_rules.what: If the capability table can answer whether a feature exists for this product and licence, answer from it and do not search.
evidence_rules.why: Deterministic and always correct, where retrieval is neither.

_conditional: A fact may depend on another. When the fact it depends on is unknown, its question is asked with a conditional prefix so the customer still answers in one reply. When that fact is known and does not match, the question is dropped entirely.

fact_labels.recent_change: what changed, and did it ever work
fact_labels.device_count: how many devices are registered, and the licence limit

_output_audience: The engine's output is for the support engineer, not the customer. Facts are split into what the engineer can look up internally and what only the customer can answer. Customer-facing wording is a separate, later concern.

_cue_decisions.reason: the licence name Limited-Log contains it, so a capability question about licences was classified as a log fault and three irrelevant questions were put to the customer (test case T1)
_cue_decisions.kept: the Japanese cue ログ, which does not collide

_cue_decisions.reason: the dependency said skip this when the vendor is known, but the intent was ask this only when SNMP is in play. On a real SNMP fault with a known vendor it stayed silent about the one fact that decides the case (test case K1).

_cue_decisions.action: three problem types added, recent_change removed from unknown_fallback
_cue_decisions.reason: four real inquiries were run through the engine on 17 Nov 2026 and three of the four were not recognised. The nine original types came from reading documentation, which describes faults. Real customers also ask about procedures, concepts and limits. The fallback was telling the customer to explain what changed on a question about a device limit, where nothing had changed.
_cue_decisions.provenance: real inquiries, not derived from the corpus
